First and foremost, mission structure.
There is extremely little variance in the structure of your objectives throughout most of the game. It basically consists of "go to location, let the Ghost access something, kill waves of enemies, (possibly repeating the first two or three steps a couple of times), interact with the Ghost to complete mission". Patrol missions consist of "kill x number of enemies", "kill a specific target", a boring "go to location and interact", an even more boring "go to location and stand for a couple seconds", and the utterly overused "collect x number of special item drops". Extremely uninspired and has been done to death for probably twenty five years and the Patrol missions have zero impact. It does nothing to help you get invested in the game universe.

Bullet sponge opponents.
While the bosses should have more hit points than regular opponents, simply adding more hit points does not make for an interesting, difficult boss. It makes for a boring, tedious boss. Higher level opponents only have more hit points and a higher level threshold for the damage variance due to the difference in opponent-character level. Simply giving the opponents and their shields more hit points does not make them more difficult, just more tedious.

Lore.
From what I have seen there is only the tidbits you get from reading the Grimoire cards, WHICH YOU CANNOT ACCESS ANYWHERE INSIDE THE FREAKING GAME. You can't even get an overview of the current state of the game universe and basic information about the entities inhabiting it until you've unlocked enough Grimoire cards. If the lore was accessible within the game then it can be tied in strongly with the missions the player is completing. If you've never looked at the Grimoire, you'll have absolutely no context as to why you're tasked with collecting something like Docking Caps, nor of their significance in Dreg society. Without context within the lore, you might as well be collecting balls of fluff. Why do I have to go outside of the game to learn any of the lore inside the game? Again, it does nothing to help you get invested in the game universe.

Loot.
Destiny has a lot of MMO patterns but loot is rather infrequent at lower levels. The ability to get loot increases once you get more towards the end-game but that assumes one stays interested enough to get there. They say that your character can have different appearances and have the envy of other players with top tier armour. The problem with that, however, is that there are only a few armour sets that give enough to one's "light level" to be at maximum level. Therefore every maximum level character of a given class doesn't look too unique from each other. There is a huge number of armour and weapon models specifically tied to lower levels that will get discarded and almost never used.

Leveling past 20.
Note: This is apparently going to change in September to a fully straight xp accumulation system when the next expansion releases.
Leveling up to 20 is a straight up xp accumulation. Every "level" after that is dependent on the amount of "light" as a stat that your armour has. For the most part, leveling past 20 IS COMPLETELY RANDOM. There is the long grind method where you have to accumulate Vanguard/Crucible Marks and Vanguard/Crucible/Faction Reputation to purchase Legendary tier armour which has a high "light stat" attached. With that armour equipped you'll have a high enough "light level" to enter end-game content to get armour that has an even higher "light stat", again random for the most part. Luck should never be included in acquiring levels.

Power creep. As it currently stands, Uncommon tier weapons have less attack than rare. Rare has less than Legendary. Legendary caps at the same level as Exotic. This cap has kept increasing with each expansion. The upcoming expansion will inject a huge amount of power creep in that the Legendary tier weapons are said to become ineffective two to three levels into the expansion and will have absolutely no method to scale up. This will also mean that older end-game content is set to become obsolete and forgotten.

Many things, and this is from someone who played like crazy, gained and maxed the best gears in the game, etc, etc... Please keep in mind I stopped playing just before the House Wolves patch, maybe some arguments are outdated.

Now:

  • Story: nothing really happens, if it did you don't know. This is particularly bad when you consider the awesome settings.

  • Reading the story: Seriously? You need to stop playing and log into their website and read the (little) story behind the game?

  • Characters: Again, nothing interesting, mostly thanks to the lack of story.

  • Lack of content: You will be grinding the same stuff over and over again way too soon and the loot is mostly painful.

  • Poor end game: Again, lack of content, more grind... but this time you are doing raids.

  • Bad loot: It's simple, the loot in this game is terrible. There is no real satisfactory progression. If you can't find a good party to do the raids, you are extremely limited and you will be grinding for toys with a once in week chance to get something not so shitty.

  • DLC: Ridiculous price and poorly implemented. Bug ridden, that splits the player base and worse, it even steals content from those that actually paid for it. (Remember the weeklies and nightfalls that were unplayable by those that didn't pay for the DLC?)

Naturally the game has some good things, the basic gameplay is superb and raids are one of the most entertaining experiences I have had in a long time.

So basically, to improve the destiny experience you need content. Also, some decency pricing the DLC and common sense with several decisions with it.

With all this said, I doubt I'll return or even touch a sequel.
